what_happened: The person running Athena edited the time limits in athena.toml by hand, outside a job. The repository tests pin the old values: two config.rs tests (the hard-jobs caps test and its budget test) and run/tests.rs a_check_killed_at_its_deadline_closes_as_an_environment_stop. The edit therefore made the base fail its tests. The person reverted it to reader 300, producer 5400, verifier 3600, check 1800, planner 600 and critic 600 seconds. The request to drop the limits now goes to Athena as a job that changes config and tests together.
cause: Tests assert exact values read from the live athena.toml, so the config and its tests form a coupled pair that a direct edit can't change one side of. Nothing warns the person editing, or runs the tests, before a hand edit of athena.toml is committed. Limit changes are only safe as a job that edits config and tests together, and that rule exists only as a convention the person has to remember.
other_causes: The pinned values are in tests outside the config file, so a person reading athena.toml can't see that those tests depend on it.
Hand edits of governed config outside a job skip the repo checks. This is the same gap seen in the hand-commit and hand-edit classes.
open_hypotheses: The input doesn't say whether the hand change was committed to main or only left in the working tree, or whether any job was rejected because of it.
The input doesn't say whether the person knew the tests pinned these values before editing.
contradictions: The registry class describes a test pinning a value derived from the live config. Here the tests pin explicit caps, so the match is on the shared cause (config and tests drift), not on identical wording.
The earlier cases are all config mistakes, but none of them involves a test pinning a config value, so none is in the same class.
prevention: Add a check that runs the config-pinning tests before any commit that touches athena.toml, and refuses a hand commit that fails them. A pre-commit or intervene step would do this. Separately, make the pinned tests read their expected values from one named source, so that a limit change is a single job that edits config and tests together.
proposed_request: Add a code check so that any commit that changes athena.toml, including a hand commit made with `athena intervene`, first runs the config-pinning tests (config.rs the_repository_config_plans_hard_jobs_only_with_the_designs_caps and its budget test, and run/tests.rs a_check_killed_at_its_deadline_closes_as_an_environment_stop). If any of them fail, the commit is refused and the failing test names are shown. Acceptance: a test shows a commit that changes a pinned time limit is refused with the failing test named, and a commit with matching config and test changes is accepted. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry. Then, as a separate job, change the reader, producer, verifier, check, planner and critic time limits as Sri requested, updating the pinned tests in the same change.
